The governing distance is the trace figure, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip record: under POL-RD-01 gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs where the two disagree, so the actual distance is 23.97 km against a booked optimal of 18.0 km — a measured excess of 5.97 km. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass on those figures: the excess is 33.17% of the 18.0 km optimal route, above the 20% test, and 5.97 km in absolute terms, above the 0.8 km test. The route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace and limb (b) of POL-RD-08 is satisfied.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 241 fixes at a 10 second sample interval across 100% coverage, no gaps at all and max_gap_sec of 0.0, and no consecutive-fix jump anywhere near the 500 m limb. No independent corroboration is therefore required for the deviation and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The only exculpatory route open to the driver is POL-RD-03, and it cannot run. I disclose that the artifact is impaired: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, with no payload — no LTA advisory covers the AYE, the PIE or the Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. POL-RD-03 needs a traffic_advisory naming an affected segment with an overlapping validity window; its absence is itself citable and it exonerates nothing. The driver's own statement concedes he knows of no advisory.

POL-RD-04 does not apply either. The two-message chat log shows the rider challenging the route — 'adam road?? jurong is the other way' at 18:58:40 — and the driver answering 'AYE jam boss, this way faster' at 18:59:20, which is an admission that the driver chose the corridor. There is no rider instruction, no named road requested by the rider, and waypoint_hint is null, so the rider-requested-detour clause is unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

Nor was either endpoint amended: amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null and no pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at is recorded, so POL-RD-05 has no amended re-quote to re-price the trip against and cannot excuse any part of the 5.97 km excess.

The fare model on this trip is METERED, so the remedy is the arithmetic of POL-RD-02, not a discretionary payment. ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this is a route-deviation dispute on trip TRP-00114 (Bugis Junction to Jurong East, 7 Aug 2026). The rider's claim succeeds in part; the driver's explanation of the detour is not supported by the record.

THE DEVIATION. gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs (POL-RD-01). The trace (EV-GPS-00114, weight 1.0; 241 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps) measures 23.97 km against the 18.0 km booked optimal on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00114, weight 1.0). The excess is 5.97 km, or 33.17%, clearing both POL-RD-01 gates (20% and 0.8 km): the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not MATERIAL (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06's driver-profile consultation, its FULL_REFUND uplift and its conduct referral are not engaged; on the citable figures there is no repeat pattern in any event (deviation_flags_90d of 1 against 412 completed trips in 90 days). The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used; the claim mentioning it did so only to exclude it, so nothing is discarded on that account.

THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC GROUND. You say the AYE was crawling from the Alexandra exit and that you went up and over on the PIE, and you accept you know of no advisory. POL-RD-03 exonerates a deviation only where a traffic advisory names the affected segment, has a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows you reaching it, and the actual route leaves and rejoins the optimal corridor. No such advisory exists: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload). Your point is therefore a general assertion of bad traffic with no artifact behind it; under POL-RD-08 it does not discharge your burden here. It is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation: that trigger requires an exculpatory clause invoked in reliance on a cited artifact that is missing, and none was relied on — the absent advisory carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)); only its absence is citable. I therefore rule on the record rather than holding it. POL-RD-04 (rider-requested detour) and POL-RD-05 (endpoint amendment) do not apply either: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00114) records no rider instruction and waypoint_hint is null, and no endpoint was amended.

THE FARE RECOMPUTATION (POL-RD-02; fare_model METERED). The multiplier 1.6 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (EV-FARE-00114) and is carried into the recomputed fare; it does not touch the 4.50 of ERP.
- charged_total: SGD 58.10
- recomputed_fare: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30) x 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 optimal-route ERP = SGD 44.42
- refund: 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded UP to SGD 13.70

The off-route Adam Road gantry charge of 2.00 is ALREADY comprehended in that refund (the recomputation credits only the on-route Kim Keat Link gantry of 2.50) and is itemised for transparency only; it must never be added on top (POL-RD-09(1)). Both gantries are matched crossings — the trace passes within 250 m of each (0.0 m and 8.76 m) — so there is no phantom line and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral. The outcome for this rider-filed dispute is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.70.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
